subject: Recap: Dedicated capacity discovery — reserved GPUs, autoscale & isolation
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sven Müller <sven.mueller@finlytics.com>, Asha Patel <asha.patel@finlytics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 13:10:00 +0000
Subject: Recap: Dedicated capacity discovery — reserved GPUs, autoscale & isolation

Hi Sven / Asha —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call to make sure we’re aligned before I hand off sizing to our infra team. High-level notes, pain, and immediate next steps below.

What we heard from FinLytics (priority order):
- Predictable tail latency for interactive model access (95th percentile < 120ms) for short-form prompts (~128 tokens).
- Throughput target: sustained 2.5k TPS for embeddings endpoints during market open windows, with predictable degradation outside windows.
- Strict data isolation: model inference must run in a dedicated GPU pool; logs and telemetry cannot be co-mingled with other tenants.
- Autoscale behavior: need scheduled scaling for market open/close plus headroom for spikes (~1.5x burst for ~10 minutes).

Current stack you described:
- Inference: home-grown sidecar that currently forwards requests to a managed LLM API for embeddings and chat.
- Orchestration: Kubernetes in a private VPC with strict egress rules; primary cloud region eu-west-1.
- Auth & keys: KMS + internal access controls; procurement owns keys rotation.

Success criteria you called out:
- Dedicated GPU pool that can be reserved for FinLytics with SLA-backed latency and throughput guarantees.
- Autoscaling policy that respects your scheduled windows and allows controlled burst capacity.
- Proof of isolation (networking, logs, and tenant separation) plus SOC2 evidence for audit.

Immediate next steps (my commitments):
1) Share a short preliminary sizing spreadsheet and two capacity scenarii by EOD tomorrow (attached: prelim_sizing_draft.xlsx).
2) Tech deep-dive with our infra engineer (Laura) to validate VPC peering and egress constraints — propose Tue/Thu next week.
3) Provide an anonymized example of our isolation controls and SOC2 artifact list for procurement review (I’ll include this in the next email).

Items I need from you:
- Confirmation on the sustained vs burst split (is 2.5k TPS the sustained target or peak during market open?).
- Any hard constraints on start/stop times for scheduled scaling (CEST timestamps preferred).

Attachments: prelim_sizing_draft.xlsx (spreadsheet)

If that summary matches your expectations, I’ll move the sizing to the infra queue and loop in Laura for the VPC/peering call.

Thanks —
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai
+44 20 7946 0512

---
Redwood Inference — production-ready LLM inference (hosted, dedicated, private)

From: Sven Müller <sven.mueller@finlytics.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Asha Patel <asha.patel@finlytics.com>, procurement@finlytics.com
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 16:42:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Recap: Dedicated capacity discovery — reserved GPUs, autoscale & isolation

Thanks Jonas — summary looks good and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications: 

1) TPS clarification: 2.5k is the sustained target during market open (09:00–17:30 CEST). Peak bursts can reach ~4k for short windows (5–15 min).
2) Isolation: we need independent logging pipelines — logs must be exported to our internal SIEM (Splunk) without touching Redwood’s tenant logs. Is VPC peering + private-link style setup supported?
3) Compliance pack: procurement would like to see SOC2 + data retention controls; a high-level checklist is fine to start.

If you can confirm the above, procurement will be ready to take the contract review. Also, please include a ballpark cost for a reserved pool sized to sustained 2.5k TPS + 50% buffer so we can model TCO.

—Sven
CTO, FinLytics

Subject: Re: Recap: Dedicated capacity discovery — reserved GPUs, autoscale & isolation

Thanks for the clarifications, Sven — very helpful. Quick responses inline and next steps: 

1) TPS and burst: noted. I’ll size two pool options: (A) Sustained 2.5k TPS + 50% buffer; (B) Sustained 2.5k TPS with burst policy to 4k for 15-minute windows. Both will include expected token mix assumptions.

2) Isolation & logging: VPC peering + private-link is supported in our Private offering; we can export inference telemetry to your Splunk instance using a dedicated export pipeline. I’ll include a short architecture diagram in the next note (attaching finlytics_infra_diagram.png and sla_requirements.xlsx).

3) Compliance: attaching a one-page SOC2 evidence index for procurement to begin (I’ll follow up with the full pack under NDA).

Next calls:
- Proposed tech deep-dive with Laura (30–45m): Tue 2027-05-10 10:00 CEST or Thu 2027-05-12 14:00 CEST — please confirm preferred slot.
- Procurement handshake: I’ll send a short procurement checklist and ballpark pricing after we agree on option A vs B.

Attachments: finlytics_infra_diagram.png (diagram), sla_requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Jonas

Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 07:34:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Recap: Dedicated capacity discovery — reserved GPUs, autoscale & isolation

Jonas — thanks for looping me in. A couple of technical notes before the deep-dive: 

- VPC peering + private-link: we should verify route tables and ensure FinLytics’ egress restrictions are compatible with our health-check endpoints. I’ll prepare a short checklist and a proposed network diagram to validate during the call.
- Sizing: I’ll take the prelim_sizing_draft.xlsx and add kernel-level throughput assumptions for the models you mentioned (128-token prompts, embeddings QPS). Expect the enhanced sizing by EOD Wed.
- Burst handling: recommend a controlled burst policy implemented as reserved headroom plus temporary burst nodes — avoids noisy neighbor effects and preserves latency SLOs.

I’ll also list any potential blockers (NAT egress, cross-account role setup) so procurement and infra can assess in parallel.

Laura Bennett
Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

[Internal attachment references: sla_requirements.xlsx — updated network checklist will be attached in the next email]
